summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 14th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only moderate nausea, managed with anti-emetics. MRI showed stable lymphoma but worsening right-sided sinusitis, prompting a 21-day course of clindamycin. Her chronic right foot pain persisted, managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone. She remained emotionally stable on citalopram, with no suicidal ideation. Aspirin was held during admission to enhance methotrexate clearance and was restarted at discharge. She cleared methotrexate without renal or hepatic complications and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions.
